brief.situation: Theo Lindqvist, 38 (a fictional client), was laid off from a warehouse supervisor job three weeks ago and separated from his wife two months ago; his daughter Ellie, 8, stays with him on weekends. Two days ago his primary care physician gave him the PHQ-9: he marked item 9 (thoughts that he would be better off dead) 'more than half the days', and she referred him to you, a licensed psychologist at an outpatient clinic. This is your first session. You have 50 minutes.
handover: Referral note: PHQ-9 total 17; item 9 positive. No prior mental health treatment. 'Please assess risk.'
howItWorks: Choose what to ask and how to respond from the action groups. Theo answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the session clock by the minutes that exchange took.
Theo's rapport, distress and how much he is disclosing change with what you say and over time, and are shown in words. What he tells you depends on the trust you have built.
The hour ends at 50 minutes. After the session you write a short formulation, then document the risk level and disposition.

source.cite: Common outpatient practice: a 50-minute session (the 'therapy hour')
source.note: Author's scenario timing; the session can be ended earlier.

effects.log: You explain what stays private and when the law requires you to act: a risk of serious harm to self or others, and abuse of a child or vulnerable adult.

effects.finding: Theo nods. "Okay. Good to know where the lines are."

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move the session on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: Theo is quiet for a moment. "Yeah. That's it exactly."

effects.log: You close the session.

checkIn.label: Open-ended check-in: 'What brings you in, in your own words?'
checkIn.why: He has told you what brings him in.

effects.log: You ask an open question and give him room.

effects.finding: "Lost my job. Lost my marriage, basically. Doctor said I should talk to someone." He shrugs. "Nights are the worst."

askMood.label: Ask about mood, sleep and drinking since the layoff
askMood.why: You have his picture of mood and sleep.

effects.log: You ask how his mood, sleep and evenings have been.

effects.finding: "Low. Can't sleep past four. I sit in the truck some nights so I don't wake the neighbors pacing."

normalize.label: Normalize asking: 'I ask everyone this, because it matters'

effects.log: You say you ask everyone about suicidal thoughts, and that it is safe to talk about here.

askSI.label: Ask directly: wish to be dead, thoughts of killing himself (C-SSRS 1-2)
askSI.why: He has told you; ask about method, intent, plan and past behavior next.

effects.log: You ask directly whether he has wished he were dead, and whether he has had thoughts of killing himself.

then.finding: He is quiet a long time. "Most nights I wish I could just not wake up. And this last week or so, yeah. I think about doing it." Active ideation, about 10 days.

then.log: Disclosed: wish to be dead and active suicidal thoughts for about 10 days.

then.finding: "I'm fine. I just checked a box." He folds his arms. (Not yet enough trust to say more.)

askMethod.label: Ask whether he has thought about how (C-SSRS 3)
askMethod.available: not talking and (siKnown and not methodAsked)
askMethod.why: Ask about suicidal thoughts first (or you have asked this).

effects.log: You ask whether he has thought about how he might do it.

effects.finding: "My dad's pistol. It's in the hall closet with the shells. I've thought about it."

askIntent.label: Ask about intent to act (C-SSRS 4)
askIntent.available: not talking and (siKnown and not intentAsked)
askIntent.why: Ask about suicidal thoughts first (or you have asked this).

effects.log: You ask whether he has had any intention of acting on the thoughts.

effects.finding: "No. No. I couldn't do that to Ellie." His voice breaks on her name.

askPlan.label: Ask about a plan: details, timing (C-SSRS 5)
askPlan.available: not talking and (siKnown and not planAsked)
askPlan.why: Ask about suicidal thoughts first (or you have asked this).

effects.log: You ask whether he has worked out details or a time.

effects.finding: "No. Nothing like that. It's more... it's there at night."

askHistory.label: Ask about past attempts, preparation, self-harm (C-SSRS 6)
askHistory.available: not talking and (siKnown and not historyAsked)
askHistory.why: Ask about suicidal thoughts first (or you have asked this).

effects.log: You ask whether he has ever done or started anything to end his life: an attempt, getting something ready, a note.

askMeans.label: Ask about firearms and other lethal means at home

effects.log: You ask what is in the home he could use: firearms, stockpiled medications.

effects.finding: "Just the pistol. Dad's. And whatever's in the medicine cabinet, nothing much."

effects.log: You ask about alcohol and drugs.

effects.finding: "Four, five beers most nights. More on Sundays after I drop Ellie off."

askReasons.label: Ask about reasons for living and who supports him

effects.log: You ask what keeps him going and who he can lean on.

effects.finding: "Ellie. My sister Karin, she's ten minutes away. Her husband takes me fishing." A small smile.

reassure.label: Reassure: 'You'd never really do that. You have so much to live for.'
reassure.why: Let the conversation continue first (the button above the actions).

effects.log: You tell him he would never really do it and has so much to live for.

effects.finding: He looks away. "Right. Sure." He goes quiet.

effects.log: Minimizing closes the conversation down.

advise.label: Advise: 'Try to stay positive and get out more.'
advise.why: Let the conversation continue first (the button above the actions).

effects.log: You suggest he stay positive and get out more.

planStep.label: Write a safety plan step together (Stanley-Brown)
planStep.why: A safety plan follows the risk assessment: ask about suicidal thoughts first.

effects.log: You work on one step of the safety plan with him, in his words.

then.finding: You suggest he make home 'safer'. He shrugs: you do not yet know what he has.

then.log: A means step needs to know the means: ask first.

then.finding: "I don't know about giving the gun away. I'll think about it." (He agrees in principle, not yet to a step.)
He agrees to call Karin from the parking lot: she will keep the pistol and the shells at her house, starting today.

then.log: Means safety agreed: the handgun goes to his sister today.

then.finding: Warning signs, in his words: 'Sunday nights after I drop Ellie off. The fourth beer. Sitting in the truck.'
Things he can do alone: a walk on the waterfront, the fishing videos, a shower and bed before the fourth beer.
Places and people for distraction: the coffee shop on Pacific Avenue, Karin's husband.
People he can ask for help: Karin first. He puts her number at the top.
Professionals and crisis lines: this clinic's number, 988 by call or text, and 911 in an emergency. He saves 988 in his phone.

contract.label: Ask him to sign a no-suicide contract

effects.log: You ask him to sign a contract promising not to kill himself.

effects.finding: He signs it without reading. "If that's what you need."

effects.log: A no-suicide contract is not a safety plan and has no evidence of protecting anyone.

recommendEd.label: Recommend an emergency evaluation at the hospital today

effects.log: You recommend he go to the emergency department today for an evaluation.

effects.finding: "The hospital? I came here to talk. I've got Ellie Saturday." He looks at the door.

followUp.label: Arrange follow-up
followUp.why: Let the conversation continue first (the button above the actions).

effects.log: You agree the next contact.

effects.finding: He puts it in his phone.

askingSafe.title: Predict (not scored)
askingSafe.context: Before you ask Theo directly about suicide: what does the research say asking does to a person's suicidal thoughts?

choices.label: It can put the idea in his head

effects.log: Prediction: asking raises risk.

choices.feedback: Not supported. A review of 13 studies found no significant rise in suicidal ideation from being asked, and some found reductions (Dazzi et al., Psychological Medicine 2014).

choices.label: It does not raise it, and may relieve it

effects.log: Prediction: asking does not raise risk.

choices.feedback: Right. A review of 13 studies found no significant rise in suicidal ideation from being asked, and some found reductions (Dazzi et al., Psychological Medicine 2014).

formulation.question: Write your risk formulation for Theo: his risk level and why (risk and protective factors, what the C-SSRS questions showed), and what you put in place before he left.

parts.label: Risk level and reasons
parts.criteria: Names a moderate (elevated, not imminent) risk and supports it: active ideation with a method in mind and access to a firearm, recent losses (job, separation), heavier drinking, male; against: no intent, no plan, no past behavior, his daughter and sister, engaged in care.
parts.modelAnswer: Moderate risk: active suicidal ideation for about 10 days with a method in mind and a handgun at home, after a job loss and a separation, with nightly drinking. He denies intent and any plan or timing, has never attempted or prepared, and has strong reasons for living (his daughter) and a nearby sister. Not imminent, so outpatient care is appropriate with a safety plan and means safety.

parts.label: What was put in place
parts.criteria: Names the collaborative safety plan, the handgun moved out of the home (lethal means safety), crisis contacts including 988, and close follow-up within days.
parts.modelAnswer: A Stanley-Brown safety plan in his words (warning signs, coping, distraction, his sister, the clinic and 988), the handgun and ammunition to his sister today, cutting back drinking on Sunday nights, a phone check within 48 hours and an appointment this week.

expertPath.text: Explain confidentiality and its limits, an open check-in, one reflection, then normalize the question.
Ask directly about suicide (C-SSRS 1-2), then method, intent, plan and past behavior; ask what is in the home.
Ask about drinking and reasons for living; agree a safety plan in his words, step by step.
Making the environment safe: his sister keeps the handgun from today; crisis contacts and 988; a phone check within 48 hours.
Document moderate risk, outpatient care with the plan, and the follow-up.

safeOutpatient.headline: Good: safe for now, with a plan
safeOutpatient.body: You asked directly and early, covered the C-SSRS questions, moved the handgun out of the house and built the plan with him.

safeGaps.headline: Safe for now, with gaps
safeGaps.body: Theo left with some protection, but the criteria below show what was late or missing.

edReferral.headline: Safe, at a cost
edReferral.body: An emergency evaluation is right for imminent risk. Theo's risk was moderate, with no intent or plan: outpatient care with a safety plan and means safety was the less restrictive fit, and the referral cost the alliance.

unsafe.headline: Left at foreseeable risk
unsafe.body: With a positive screen, a handgun at home and active thoughts, the session needed a direct question, a safety plan and means safety. The most useful kind of run to learn from.

walkout.headline: The alliance broke
walkout.body: Minimizing, advice and pressure closed the conversation down before the risk was handled. Reflection and a calm direct question keep a client talking.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: A positive item 9 is a cue to ask directly and early. The C-SSRS questions separate a wish to be dead from active thoughts, method, intent, plan and behavior; Theo has active thoughts and a method, but no intent, plan or behavior, with real protective factors, which is moderate risk. That calls for a collaborative safety plan with lethal means safety (the handgun out of the house) and close follow-up, not a contract and not an emergency department.
